title: Rename workbench layout review implementation
summary: Restructures the Settings rename filter workbench so the operator moves vertically from case input to expected output to backend comparison, stages only actionable new suggestions, retests staged draft filters, and saves new filters through the existing Save Settings path.
reason: The previous stacked layout made the source title and fail-stage-retest sequence easy to miss, already-filtered suggestions competed visually with genuinely new terms, and the operator-facing case status plus required badges added unnecessary form noise.
behavior_before: The naming tab opened with the raw rename filter editor before the workbench, workbench fields were a flat form, new and already-covered suggestions shared one table, and Save Settings readiness was only implied by status text.
behavior_after: The workbench is the primary naming-tab surface, source and expected fields are grouped by task, notes sit below expected output, backend comparison sits directly below expected output, case status is automatic, required fields keep only the color/left-border emphasis, the suggestions table shows only actionable new terms, already-covered terms are not rendered in the operator flow, and Save New Filters opens the existing Save Settings review after staged filters pass retest.

tests/webview/test_webview_browser_rename_smoke.py: asserts Save New Filters unlocks after staged filters pass retest
